evidence_quote: The research to date has shown that the flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity.
finding: FLEX found that heptane and methanol fuel droplets diluted with inert suppressant gases keep burning at a lower flammability limit in reduced gravity than in normal gravity.
conditions: Reduced gravity; oxygen-nitrogen mixtures diluted with an inert gas
earth_comparison: The flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity than in normal gravity.

team_interpretation.text: Suppression levels proven on Earth may not be enough in space.

score_reasons.crew_safety: Fires may survive conditions that would stop them on Earth.
score_reasons.evidence: ISS results summarized by NASA in an official guide.
score_reasons.moon_mars: Applies to any low-gravity vehicle or habitat.

evidence_quote: The implication is that terrestrial standards for inert gas suppressants in low gravity do not offer the same margin of safety as in normal gravity.
finding: Because flammability limits are lower in reduced gravity, inert-gas suppressant standards developed on Earth do not give the same margin of safety in low gravity.
earth_comparison: Earth (terrestrial) standards for inert gas suppressants give a smaller safety margin in low gravity.

team_interpretation.text: Inert-gas fire suppression in spacecraft should be sized with space data, not only Earth standards.

score_reasons.crew_safety: Directly about how much suppressant is enough.
score_reasons.evidence: NASA's stated implication of the FLEX results.
score_reasons.moon_mars: Fire suppression design for exploration vehicles.

evidence_quote: identified an LOI that is both significantly lower than in normal gravity and lower than previously predicted and anticipated
finding: FLEX identified a limiting oxygen index (the lowest oxygen level that supports burning) for heptane and methanol droplets that is significantly lower than in normal gravity and lower than predicted.
earth_comparison: The limiting oxygen index is significantly lower than in normal gravity.

team_interpretation.text: Lowering cabin oxygen gives less fire protection in space than Earth data suggest.

score_reasons.crew_safety: Fuels can burn at lower oxygen in space than expected.
score_reasons.evidence: Measured on the ISS; summarized by NASA.

evidence_quote: The FLEX tests showed that the cool flame can burn for a prolonged period of time.
finding: After the visible hot flame of a fuel droplet went out, a low-temperature 'cool flame' kept burning for a prolonged period, which many researchers had thought impossible.

team_interpretation.text: After a fire seems extinguished, crews should keep monitoring: burning can continue without a visible flame.

score_reasons.crew_safety: A fire that looks out may not be out.
score_reasons.evidence: Unexpected ISS result, later explained and accepted.

evidence_quote: persistent flames, invisible to the unaided eye, that will spontaneously re-ignite long after the visible flame has been extinguished.
finding: Reduced gravity is particularly conducive to very weak but persistent flames, invisible to the eye, that can spontaneously re-ignite long after the visible flame has been put out.

team_interpretation.text: Post-fire monitoring should use instruments, not only eyes, in case of invisible flames.

open_question: What conditions let an invisible cool flame spontaneously re-ignite after the visible flame is out? NASA says the pre-conditions, chemistry and mechanisms are poorly understood.

score_reasons.crew_safety: Invisible re-ignition risk after a fire.
score_reasons.evidence: NASA guide statement linked to FLEX cool-flame findings.

evidence_quote: The goal of the research is to examine how the addition of an inert gas suppressant influences the flammability limit of the two fuels.
finding: FLEX burned heptane and methanol droplets in oxygen-nitrogen mixtures diluted with nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon to see how inert suppressant gases change flammability limits.
conditions: Inert gases tested: nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium, xenon

score_reasons.crew_safety: Explains what the suppressant results are based on.
score_reasons.moon_mars: Gas suppressants are candidates for future vehicles.
